body.p: The thermal solution must provide less than 800 PSI on average, for any 2 mm x 2 mm square region on the die complex.

section.title: Notes on Maximum Allowable Die Pressure

ul.li: During or after thermal solution assembly, disassembly, test, or rework, Intel component dies may be inadvertently subjected to a high concentrated load, resulting in a risk of die damage. For more discussion of these risks, and precautions that can be taken to reduce the risk of die damage, see Section 4.6.2.

Intel recommends that customers validate their thermal solution assembly to ensure that the allowable maximum pressure is never exceeded at any 2mm x 2mm location on the die, at any instant during or after assembly/disassembly of the thermal solution.
Transient compressive pressure refers to the momentary pressure at any 2mm x 2mm location on the die during the thermal solution assembly or disassembly (see figure below).
Static compressive pressure refers to the long-term maximum pressure at any 2mm x 2mm location on the die after installation of the thermal solution is completed (see figure below).
An ideal thermal solution design will have a transient pressure that is less than or equal to the long-term static pressure on the die.
However, in practice, not all thermal solution designs will achieve this ideal, and may have a transient pressure that is higher than the static pressure.
Therefore, Intel recommends validating each thermal solution design for both transient and static pressure, to ensure that the maximum allowable pressure on the die is never exceeded at any time.
For guidance on experimental measurement of die pressure, refer to Intel® Mobile SoC Die Loading Measurement Techniques, (#556532).
For guidance on the use of structural simulation to predict both static and transient die pressures, refer to Mobile Thermal Attach Structural Modeling (#575675).
